paras: The killing of T. J. Thomas was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Mounted Policeman Jesse F. Greek at Jacksonville on the night of Wednesday, December 9, 1903. According to the only report found, Greek fired after Thomas came at him with an open razor during a quarrel, and the story ran as a brief item in the Savannah Morning News two days later.

Thomas, described as "a negro," was quarreling with another Black man and held an open razor in his right hand. Greek, told of the fight, went to stop it and caught the razor, cutting his hand "very painfully," and then threw Thomas to the ground. In this account Thomas got up and came at the officer with the razor, and Greek drew his revolver and fired several times. One shot struck Thomas in the breast, and he was killed.
No report of an inquest, charge or departmental inquiry into the shooting appears in the coverage found.

The Savannah Morning News carried the story on December 11 under the headline "KILLED BY A POLICEMAN," on page 10. The item identified Thomas by race and set out the policeman's justification as plain narrative, naming no witness and giving no other version. No Jacksonville paper, later follow-up or Black-press account of the shooting was found.
